faqs.question: Is शुभ दीपावली correct Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: It is correct Hindi, but in Sanskrit the adjective has to agree with the feminine noun, so write शुभा दीपावलिः as a phrase or शुभदीपावलिः as one compound. Monier-Williams spells the noun dīpāvali, with a short i. The full wish दीपावलिः शुभा भवतु (dīpāvaliḥ śubhā bhavatu) means "may Diwali be bright and auspicious".

faqs.question: Which Sanskrit shloka is best for a Diwali card?
faqs.answer: Bhagavad Gita 10.11, the "lamp of knowledge" verse: तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥ At 32 syllables it is too long for a status but right for a card, and Edwin Arnold's 1885 translation gives you an English line to print beneath it.

faqs.question: Is Deepavali spelt with a long ī or a short i in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: Monier-Williams's 1899 dictionary lists dīpāvali (दीपावलि) with a short final i on page 481, meaning "a row of lights, nocturnal illumination". The long-ī दीपावली is the Hindi spelling and is not a headword there. For a Sanskrit line, use दीपावलिः in the nominative.

faqs.question: Is शुभं करोति कल्याणम् a Vedic mantra?
faqs.answer: We could not trace it to a public-domain edition with a verse number, so treat it as a household lamp prayer rather than a Vedic text. If you use it, check three words that ranking pages misspell: आरोग्यम् with a long ā, विनाशाय without a visarga, and दीपज्योतिः as one compound.

faqs.question: How do I wish my parents Happy Diwali in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: Use the dual, the Sanskrit form for exactly two people: चिरं जीवतं सुखिनौ भवतम् (ciraṃ jīvataṃ sukhinau bhavatam), "live long, both of you, and be happy". A mother and father together take the masculine dual सुखिनौ. For three or more people, switch to चिरं जीवत सुखिनो भवत.

faqs.question: Can I write my own Diwali wish in Sanskrit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you check every word in a dictionary such as Monier-Williams and use the imperative ending -tu or -tām for "may it be". Avoid forms like भविष्यतु, which appear on ranking pages but are not Sanskrit verbs. If the line is going into a card, ask someone who reads Sanskrit to look at it once.

faqs.question: What is a short Sanskrit Diwali status?
faqs.answer: तमो नश्यतु, ज्योतिर्वर्धताम् (tamo naśyatu, jyotir vardhatām), "let the dark be lost; let the light grow", is five words. For a classical line, the first half of Bhagavata Purana 4.21.4, प्रजास्तं दीपबलिभिः संभृताशेषमङ्गलैः, is 16 syllables about a city meeting its king with lamps.

faqs.question: Which Sanskrit wish suits a client or business contact?
faqs.answer: भवतो व्यापारो वर्धताम् (bhavato vyāpāro vardhatām), "may your business grow", is polite and short. For an elder in business, the Isha Upanishad's verse 18, "Agni, lead us on to wealth by a good path", asks for wealth and an honest road to it in one line.

faqs.question: How do I pronounce the ḥ at the end of dīpāvaliḥ?
faqs.answer: The ḥ is visarga, a soft breath that echoes the vowel before it, so dīpāvaliḥ ends roughly "-li-hi". Read ś and ṣ close to "sh", ṃ as a nasal hum, and hold barred vowels such as ā and ī about twice as long.

faqs.question: Can I put a Sanskrit shloka on a SubhSandesh Diwali page?
faqs.answer: Yes. On SubhSandesh's Happy Diwali page each wish diya lifts one wish you type, so one diya can carry the Devanagari line and the next its meaning. The page does not check your Sanskrit, so paste from a source you trust; 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so keep each line short.

faqs.question: When is Diwali in 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja falls on Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October and Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October. The Rigveda dawn line, "This light is come, amid all lights the fairest", fits a message on the morning after, Saturday 30 October.

# Diwali Wishes in Sanskrit: Shlokas With Verse Numbers and Every Word Checked

Of all Diwali wishes in Sanskrit, the shortest correct one is दीपावलिः शुभा भवतु (dīpāvaliḥ śubhā bhavatu), "may this Diwali be bright and auspicious". Below are four classical lines with verse numbers, six new wishes checked in Monier-Williams, and five spelling errors to avoid. Diwali 2027 (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Friday 29 October.

Two SubhSandesh numbers shaped the format: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone (measured 24 September 2026), so every line carries Devanagari plus a Roman transliteration that survives a small screen. On Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we have measured (n = 89, so treat it as an analogue), 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself. Expect to copy these on the evening itself, so each line is ready to paste.

## What is the correct way to say Happy Diwali in Sanskrit?

Monier-Williams's 1899 Sanskrit-English Dictionary, page 481, lists [dīpāvali](https://www.sanskrit-lexicon.uni-koeln.de/scans/csl-apidev/getword.php?dict=mw&key=dIpAvali&input=slp1&output=iast) as a feminine noun, "a row of lights, nocturnal illumination", ending in a short i. Hindi's long-ī दीपावली is not a headword there.

Because śubha (page 1083, "splendid, bright, beautiful") is an adjective, it has to agree with a feminine noun as śubhā. So the Hindi habit "शुभ दीपावली" becomes either the phrase शुभा दीपावलिः or the compound शुभदीपावलिः in Sanskrit. The popular "शुभाशयाः" is modern usage: Monier-Williams glosses śubhāśaya on page 1083 as "of virtuous disposition", not "good wishes".

> दीपावलिः शुभा भवतु । (dīpāvaliḥ śubhā bhavatu) "May Diwali be bright and auspicious."

## Four classical Sanskrit lines for Diwali, with text and verse

On 22 October 2026, the four top-five pages we could open for this search gave no verse number for any shloka (the fifth refused our connection). Each line below names its verse and a public-domain translation, with the Sanskrit as printed on Sanskrit Wikisource.

### 1. Rigveda 1.113.1: "This light is come"

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।
> idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgāc citraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā

Ralph Griffith's 1896 translation of [Rigveda Book 1, Hymn 113](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Hymns_of_the_Rigveda/Book_1/Hymn_113) reads: "This light is come, amid all lights the fairest; born is the brilliant, far-extending brightness." The hymn praises Uṣas, the dawn, so it suits a message sent on the morning after Lakshmi Puja, Saturday 30 October 2027.

### 2. Isha Upanishad 18: "Lead us on to wealth by a good path"

> अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> agne naya supathā rāye asmān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān

Max Müller's 1879 translation in [Sacred Books of the East, Volume 1](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Sacred_Books_of_the_East/Volume_1/V%C3%A2gasaneyi-samhit%C3%A2-upanishad) reads: "Agni, lead us on to wealth (beatitude) by a good path, thou, O God, who knowest all things!" It suits a business owner or an elder: it asks for wealth and the right road to it at once.

### 3. Bhagavad Gita 10.11: the lamp of knowledge

> तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तमः । नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता ॥
> teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñānajaṃ tamaḥ, nāśayāmy ātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā

Edwin Arnold's 1885 verse translation, [The Song Celestial on Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2388), renders it: "And, all for love of them, within their darkened souls I dwell, And, with bright rays of wisdom's lamp, their ignorance dispel." Send it to a teacher, a mentor or a student in an exam year.

### 4. Bhagavata Purana 4.21.4: a city that met its king with lamps

> प्रजास्तं दीपबलिभिः संभृताशेषमङ्गलैः ।
> prajās taṃ dīpabalibhiḥ saṃbhṛtāśeṣamaṅgalaiḥ

In [Bhagavata Purana Book 4, Chapter 21](https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/%E0%A4%B6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0%E0%A5%80%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%A6%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%A4%E0%A4%AA%E0%A5%81%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%A3%E0%A4%AE%E0%A5%8D/%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%A7%E0%A4%83_%E0%A5%AA/%E0%A4%85%E0%A4%A7%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%AF%E0%A4%83_%E0%A5%A8%E0%A5%A7), King Prithu returns to his capital and his people come out to meet him. Our literal rendering: "the people, with offerings of lamps and every auspicious thing gathered, came to meet him". Send it to someone coming home for Diwali.

One detail no other page on this search mentions: Monier-Williams cites this very verse, BhP iv.21.4, for the word dīpāvali, while the Wikisource edition reads dīpabalibhiḥ, "with lamp offerings". Editions differ by a syllable, so quote the edition you name.

## Which classical line suits whom

Syllables are our own hand count against each metre. A half-verse is the first two quarter-lines.

| Line | Verse | Translation you can open | Syllables quoted | Best sent to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "This light is come" | Rigveda 1.113.1 | Griffith, 1896 | 22 (half-verse, trishtubh) | Anyone, the morning after Diwali |
| "Lead us on to wealth" | Isha Upanishad 18 | Müller, 1879 | 22 (half-verse, trishtubh) | A client, a shop owner, an elder |
| "Wisdom's lamp" | Bhagavad Gita 10.11 | Arnold, 1885 | 32 (full verse, anushtubh) | A teacher or a student |
| "Lamp offerings" | Bhagavata Purana 4.21.4 | Our literal rendering | 16 (half-verse, anushtubh) | Someone travelling home |

The 16-syllable Purana line fits a WhatsApp status most easily. The 32-syllable Gita verse belongs in a card.

## Six new Sanskrit Diwali wishes, every word checked

These are our own compositions, so no tradition stands behind them. Every word was checked in Monier-Williams (page numbers in brackets), and every verb is a standard imperative.

- दीपालोकेन लक्ष्मीस्ते गृहं प्रविशतु । (dīpālokena lakṣmīs te gṛhaṃ praviśatu) "By lamplight, may Lakshmi enter your home." (dīpāloka "lamp-light" 481, lakṣmī 892, gṛha 361, pra-viś "to enter" 692)
- तमो नश्यतु, ज्योतिर्वर्धताम् । (tamo naśyatu, jyotir vardhatām) "Let the dark be lost; let the light grow." (tamas 438, naś "to be lost, perish" 531, jyotis 427, vṛdh 1010)
- आरोग्यं ते सदास्तु । (ārogyaṃ te sadāstu) "May good health be yours always." (ārogya "freedom from disease, health" 151, sadā "always" 1139)
- भवतो व्यापारो वर्धताम् । (bhavato vyāpāro vardhatām) "May your business grow." For a client or a trader (vyāpāra "occupation, business" 1038).
- दीपालोकेन भवत्या गृहं प्रकाशताम् । (dīpālokena bhavatyā gṛhaṃ prakāśatām) "May your home shine with lamplight." Polite form for a woman; for a man use भवतो (bhavato). (pra-kāś "to shine" 653)
- चिरं जीव सुखी भव । (ciraṃ jīva sukhī bhava) "Live long, be happy." For one man or boy; for a woman or girl, सुखिनी भव (sukhinī bhava). (cira 398, jīv 422, sukhin "happy, joyful" 1222)

## One person, two, or a whole family: Sanskrit's three numbers

Sanskrit verbs have a dual, a form for exactly two people, which Hindi lost. Monier-Williams gives bhū, "to be", on page 760; its imperative is bhava for one person, bhavatam for two and bhavata for three or more. That makes the last wish above change shape with the audience.

- One person: चिरं जीव सुखी भव । (ciraṃ jīva sukhī bhava)
- Two people, such as your parents or a couple: चिरं जीवतं सुखिनौ भवतम् । (ciraṃ jīvataṃ sukhinau bhavatam)
- A whole family or group: चिरं जीवत सुखिनो भवत । (ciraṃ jīvata sukhino bhavata)

A mixed pair takes the masculine dual, so सुखिनौ covers mother and father together. Use the plural only for three or more.

## Five spelling errors on page one of the search results

We read the top-ranking pages for this search on 22 October 2026, and two of them carried these five errors. Here is the correct form of each, with the reason.

- दीपःज्योति should be दीपज्योतिः. Inside a compound the first word loses its ending, and jyotis ends in visarga.
- विनाशायः should be विनाशाय. It is the dative of vināśa, "for the destruction of" (page 969), with no visarga.
- अरोग्यम should be आरोग्यम्, with a long ā (page 151).
- भविष्यतु is not a verb form. Monier-Williams lists the future as bhaviṣyati; the imperative "let it be" is भवतु.
- प्रकाशित करोतु needs agreement as प्रकाशितं करोतु, or simply प्रकाशयतु, the causative "may it illumine" (page 653).

The first three come from the lamp prayer that begins शुभं करोति कल्याणम्. We could not trace that prayer to a public-domain edition with a verse number, so this post corrects its words rather than printing it as a classical citation.

## How to say a Sanskrit wish aloud

Exact recitation is a trained skill. A [2021 study in Scientific Reports](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8102627) by Kumar and colleagues recruited 25 Vedic pandits from schools around Lucknow who had begun training at 9 to 11 and trained full-time for 10 years, about 17,743 hours. It compared their brain structure with 25 matched controls; it says nothing about greetings, only how demanding exact recitation is.

You do not need that level for a wish. Read ś and ṣ roughly as "sh", ṃ as a nasal hum, and ḥ as a soft echo of the vowel before it (dīpāvaliḥ ends "-li-hi"). Long vowels with a bar, such as ā and ī, are held for about twice as long.

## Sending a Sanskrit wish on a Diwali page

The [SubhSandesh Happy Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) gives a Sanskrit line somewhere to stay: they light a diya at their door that carries your tag, then a row of wish diyas, each lifting one of your wishes, so one diya can hold दीपालोकेन लक्ष्मीस्ते गृहं प्रविशतु and the next its meaning. Your letter opens from a red-and-gold shagun liffafa, and a box of mithai ends on a Shubh Deepavali card signed by you.

It takes about five minutes, and it opens as a private link in any browser with no app or account. You can choose family, love or friend mode, add up to six photos to the sky lanterns and set an optional password, which 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators did before sharing (measured 24 September 2026).

If they would rather hear you recite the verse, [Dedication, a radio show made for one person](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication), plays your real voice introducing a song. It is not a Diwali template, but it carries a shloka in your own voice, which a typed card cannot.

## When a Sanskrit wish is the wrong choice

A recipient who does not read Devanagari gets little from a 32-syllable verse, so lead with the English and add the Sanskrit as a gift. Jain families mark Mahavira's nirvana on Diwali and Sikh families mark Bandi Chhor Divas, so a Vedic hymn to Agni may not fit them; the plain दीपावलिः शुभा भवतु does.

A Gita verse in a jokey group forward reads as careless to people who recite it daily. And the Happy Diwali page does not check your Sanskrit: whatever you type is what they read, so paste from a source you trust.
